content.text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an oxindole core.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H and is attached at its meta position to a second ring. On the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is adjacent to the C-OH carbon, and the next carbon bears the NH–N= group. So the second ring is 1-aryl, 2-OH, 3-NHN=.

**Oxindole part.**
- C3 is the C=N carbon, C2 is the C=O carbon, and N1 carries a 4-ethylphenyl group.
- The benzo ring has F at C4 (adjacent to C3a) and CF3 at C6.
- Ring order: C3a is bonded to C4(F), then C5(H), then C6(CF3), then C7(H), then C7a, which is bonded to N1.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with N at the upper left of C3 and the NH below it, but the geometry is ambiguous, so I assigned it from the layout. C3 sits at about (330, 455), with N at (300, 405) above-left and C2 to the lower left. The N substituent HN is at (210, 380) to the left. On C3, the C3a substituent is to the right, and the C2 substituent is lower left.

Writing the SMILES as C3(=N/NH...)... with C2 as the lower neighbour: the NH is on the left of N, and C2 is on the left side of C3 (lower). Both lie on the same side of the C=N axis, which is cis (Z) between NH and C2. I'll encode it that way.

SMILES: `OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(CC)cc3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(F)c23)c1O`

Check on the stereo: in `N/N=C2/C(=O)...`, the N's substituent (the preceding NH) is written before N with `/`, and C2's following substituent C(=O) is written with `/`. That means the two are trans. For cis I need `N/N=C2\C(=O)`, so I changed it.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3ccc(CC)cc3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(F)c23)c1O
